subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.

spec.name: Blueprint Spitfire
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire fighter on its landing gear, rendered as a living cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue hulls covered in white-cyan drafting linework, glowing panel seams and a gridded drafting sheet under it.
spec.layout: Museum-level stance, all three wheels resting on a flat drafting sheet at y=0; the plane itself sits level, nose to +Z. From the front: a five-blade propeller disc (r 1.65, hub centre y 1.85) on a tapered steel spinner reaching z 4.95, behind it the rounded cowling barrel (y 1.35..2.1). The low elliptical wing spans x -5.55..5.55 at y 0.95, chord 2.7 at the root tapering to a rounded 1.15 tip, with cannon barrels through the leading edge, a radiator bath under each wing and ailerons at the trailing edge. Above the wing root: an open cockpit trough at z 1.2..2.1 closed by a framed canopy whose top is y 2.45. The fuselage loft tapers from the bulged cockpit section to a slender tail cone at z -3.4, which the tail part continues to z -4.5, carrying the swept fin (top y 2.9, hinged rudder) and the elliptical tailplane with elevators. The style shows everywhere: every hull surface is flat blueprint blue (lighter on top, deeper below), panel seams, rivets, port rims and outlines are seated lineWhite strips, studs and decals, leading edges, canopy glass and hub rings glow cyan, tiny amber accents mark wingtip lights and prop-blade tips, and the sheet under the whole plane carries the grid, border, title block, dimension lines and section flags.

parts.builds: The monocoque spine from the cowling front face back to the tail cone at z -3.4. Build one loft along z from [0,1.85,3.3] to [0,1.35,-3.4]: cowling barrel widest at the nose (half-width 0.49, from y 1.35 to 2.1), slimming over the forward fuselage, a bulged cockpit section (half-width 0.5), then tapering to a slender cone (half-width 0.18) at z -3.4. Main loft hullBlue; a panelBlue band rings the cowling at z 2.9..3.3, and a deepBlue belly strip runs under the cockpit. Add a dorsal spine ridge fairing (panelBlue) along the top from z 1.0 to z -3.4. Cockpit at z 1.2..2.1: recessed trough rim, then a closed canopy — steel frame ribs, glowCyan glass panes, and lineWhite seam strips on the frames. Drafting details: five panel seam bands of thin lineWhite strips (0.012 thick, seated 0.005 proud) ringing the loft at z 2.8, 1.9, 0.9, -0.6 and -2.2, with ~50 tiny lineWhite rivet studs along them; two gun cowl ports above the cowling at z 2.55, x +/-0.28 (deepBlue discs with lineWhite rims); six exhaust stubs (steel, three per side) along the cowl sides at z 2.95..3.55 at y 1.55, raked back; a steel antenna mast on the spine at z -1.0 with a faintCyan antenna wire stub; an oil cooler scoop (deepBlue with a glowCyan grill face) under the nose at z 2.4; and a lineWhite crosshair inspection circle decal on each side of the tail cone. Attaches: its front face at z 3.3 meets the propeller at mount noseRing; its lower flanks join the wings at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; its rear face at z -3.4 hands over to the tail.
parts.attaches: Front face at mount noseRing (propeller); lower flanks at mounts wingRootL/R (wings); rear face at z -3.4 (tail).

parts.builds: Both elliptical wings, built as one piece per side with loft stations running out along x from 0.95 to 5.55: chord 2.7 at the root tapering smoothly (elliptical planform) to 1.15 at the rounded tip, thickness about 12% of chord, wing plane centred at y 0.95 with 0.06 of dihedral. Upper surfaces hullBlue, undersides deepBlue, split along the leading-edge crown line. A thin glowCyan strip runs along the leading edge of each wing. Trailing edge: ailerons (panelBlue slabs, x 3.1..5.3, offset 0.03 behind the wing with lineWhite seam gaps and small hinge studs) and inboard flaps (deepBlue, x 1.1..3.0) with the same seam treatment. Cannon: two per wing — steel barrels (r 0.045) protruding 0.5 from the leading edge at x +/-2.55 and +/-3.9, y 1.0, each with a panelBlue fairing bulge and a lineWhite port ring; two further machine-gun ports (lineWhite-rimmed deepBlue discs) at x +/-4.7. Radiator bath under each wing at x +/-1.75, z 0.35: a deepBlue scoop 0.55 long with a glowCyan grill face and a lineWhite edge. Drafting details on the upper wing: a concentric paper crosshair roundel (lineWhite rings, outer 0.9 diameter) at x +/-2.3, and ~10 small faintCyan inspection patches (thin rectangles with corner rivets) scattered on the upper skin. Tip details: amber disc lights at both wingtips, a steel pitot tube below the left (+x) tip and a faintCyan nav light disc under the right tip. Attaches: each root meets the fuselage flank at mounts wingRootL and wingRootR; the undersides at mounts gearTopL and gearTopR take the landing-gear struts.
parts.attaches: Roots at mounts wingRootL/R (fuselage); underside strut mounts gearTopL/R (landing gear).

parts.builds: Everything aft of z -3.4. First the rear fuselage cone: a continuation of the spine loft from half-width 0.18 at z -3.4 down to 0.10 at [0,1.35,-4.5], hullBlue with one lineWhite seam band and a few rivet studs. The fin: an extruded flat slab with the swept Spitfire profile, root spanning z -3.6..-4.5 at the spine, top at y 2.9, leading edge leaning back; hullBlue, with a panelBlue rudder slab hinged on the rudder joint covering the rear half of the fin, edged in lineWhite seam strips, with small lineWhite hinge studs and a lineWhite crosshair circle decal at y 2.3. A panelBlue fillet fairing blends the fin root into the spine. The tailplane: two elliptical flat slabs, each spanning out to x +/-1.85, at y 1.95, z -4.0, hullBlue on top and deepBlue below, each with a panelBlue elevator slab covering the rear 30% and lineWhite seam gaps; a lineWhite crosshair circle on the upper tailplane. A small steel rudder actuator rod runs under the tail cone. Attaches: its front face at z -3.4 meets the fuselage rear face at mount finRoot; the cone underside at mount tailwheelTop takes the tail wheel.
parts.attaches: Front face at z -3.4 (fuselage, mount finRoot); underside at mount tailwheelTop (landing gear tail wheel).

parts.builds: The propeller assembly on the propHub joint at mount noseRing [0,1.85,3.3]. Spinner: a lathe of steel, radius 0.34 at its base tapering to a blunt rounded tip at z 4.95, with a lineWhite ring at its base and a small lineWhite crosshair decal on the tip. Behind the spinner, a steel back-plate disc (r 0.4) at z 3.35 with a glowCyan hub ring. Five blades radiating from the hub, one pointing straight up, the others at 72 degree steps around the z axis: each a flat extruded blade from radius 0.3 to 1.65, 0.24 wide, twisted about 20 degrees along its length, deepBlue, with a thin lineWhite edge line on each face and the outer 0.25 of each tip painted amber. Blades are thin (0.02..0.05 thick, lens-shaped), so the disc reads as five crisp lines. Attaches: the hub root seats into the cowling front face at mount noseRing; the whole assembly rides the propHub joint.
parts.attaches: Hub root at mount noseRing (fuselage); blades spin on joint propHub.

parts.builds: The ground stance; the only aircraft part whose wheels touch the sheet at y 0. Two raked main legs, each a steel capsule strut (r 0.055) from mount gearTopL [1.6,0.9,0.8] (and mirrored gearTopR) down and outward to the axle at [2.55,0.55,0.95] (mirrored), with a thinner steel drag brace (r 0.035) from a point at z 1.35 on the wing underside back to mid-leg, plus a small faintCyan inspection band on each strut. Wheels at the axles: r 0.55, 0.18 wide tires in deepBlue with a lineWhite tread seam ring, steel hubs r 0.20 each with a lineWhite bolt circle of 8 tiny studs and one small amber greaser dot. Tail wheel: a steel leaf-spring strut (a short flat slab) from mount tailwheelTop [0,0.55,-4.05] down to the axle [0,0.2,-4.05], with a small deepBlue tire (r 0.2) and steel hub with a lineWhite stud ring. All three wheels rest exactly on the sheet; nothing else of this part goes below y 0.05. Attaches: leg tops at mounts gearTopL/R (wings); tail-wheel strut top at mount tailwheelTop (tail).
parts.attaches: Leg tops at mounts gearTopL/R (wings); tail wheel top at mount tailwheelTop (tail).

parts.builds: The cyanotype drafting sheet the plane stands on — flat slab 12.4 x 10.8 (x +/-6.2, z +/-5.4), 0.03 thick, top surface at y 0.03, in sheetBlue, with a gridCyan grid paint of 0.5 m squares and a double border frame (a lineWhite strip inside a glowCyan strip) 0.15 in from the edge, plus lineWhite corner registration crosses. Title block at the near-right corner (x 3.6..6.0, z -5.3..-3.9): ruled lineWhite rows and svg decals in lineWhite reading SUPERMARINE SPITFIRE MK.IX, PROJ 1942, SCALE 1:24, SHEET 3 OF 12, with one small amber stamp disc. Drafting overlay around the plane: one lineWhite dimension line with arrowheads running along x at z -2.2 measuring the wingspan, one lineWhite height dimension beside the nose at x 2.2 with tick marks, three circled section flags (glowCyan rings with lineWhite letters) floating beside fuselage and wing around x +/-3.4, y 2.6, and a faint glowCyan arc on the sheet at z 4.3, r 1.65, marking the propeller disc sweep. All annotation decals sit in model space on the airframe bone; the sheet itself is a static prop.
parts.attaches: Lies flat under the whole model; the three gear wheels rest on its top face at y 0.

calls.reasoning:
I need to write a spec JSON for a team building a Spitfire fighter plane in cyanotype blueprint style. Not module code — just the JSON spec.

Cyanotype blueprint style: deep Prussian blue background/ink, white/cyan line work. For a 3D model of a Spitfire in blueprint style: the plane's surfaces are deep blue with white/cyan linework, panel lines, rivets, annotations drawn as decals/parts, glowing white-cyan edges. Palette: blueprint blue (#1a3a6b or classic cyanotype #0b3d91 / #16305c), lighter blue mid tone, white line color (#eaf6ff), cyan glow (#3fd9ff), maybe accent pale. The plane stands on floor — landing gear down, so it sits on y=0 on wheels/tail skid. Real Spitfire: length ~9.1 m, wingspan ~11.2 m, height ~3.0 m (with prop). That's big. Maybe keep real-world size: 11.2 wide, 3.7 tall (prop disc), 9.8 long. That's within limits.

Spitfire layout: elliptical wings, round tail, spinner with 5-blade prop, bubble-ish canopy (Spitfire has rounded canopy), radiator under wing, exhaust stubs, roundels (could be blueprint annotation circles instead — in blueprint style, roundels as circles with crosshairs). Blueprints have title blocks, dimension lines, rivet dots, section markers.

Parts (3–6):
1. Fuselage: monocoque body, nose/engine cowling, canopy, tail boom to fin, cockpit frame.
2. Wings: elliptical wing pair, radiators, cannon, fuel vents.
3. Empennage: tail fin, rudder, horizontal stabilizers.
4. Propeller & engine front: spinner, 5 blades, exhaust stubs.
5. Landing gear: main wheels, gear struts, tail skid, ground stance.
6. Blueprint annotations: title block, dimension lines, crosshairs — but every piece must belong to exactly one part. Could make a "blueprint drafting layer" part that owns annotation overlays across the model. But box constraints — annotations span whole model. Hmm, annotations could be attached per-part. Or a 6th part "annotation overlay" with a box spanning the whole model — allowed since parts are defined by box but annotations float near the plane. Better to assign annotations to each builder's part? The spec says each part owns its details. But a drafting overlay (title block on the floor, dimension lines) — the floor rest: title block as a ground plane decal under the plane? That's scenery though — but blueprint style strongly suggests a drafting sheet background. The brief says scenery only where named; the blueprint style could name a drafting-sheet ground. I could make the floor: a large blueprint sheet with grid, title block. That's part of the pitch's style, acceptable: "its style is unmistakable." I'll make a "drafting sheet" ground plane as part 6 with floor: true, and plane parts floor: false except landing gear.

Actually "floor: true marks the parts whose lowest points rest on y = 0" — the wheels rest on y=0; the sheet at y=0 too. Fine.

Parts:
1. fuselage — spine, nose cowling, canopy, cockpit. Box roughly [-0.8, 0.9, -4.2] to [0.8, 2.4, 3.2]... Let me lay out coordinates.

Spitfire dims (scaled): length 9.2 m, height 3.7 m (prop top), wingspan 11.2 m. Center on x=0, front +Z. Let nose at z=+4.6, tail at z=-4.6. Ground y=0; wheels radius ~0.45, axle at ~1.4? Actually Spitfire main wheels are ~0.5 diameter... Let's approximate: axle height 0.75, wheel radius 0.75? Real Spitfire wheel diameter ~0.57m. Let's say wheels radius 0.55, axle at y=0.55 under wings at z≈+0.6, x≈±2.6. Tail wheel small, radius 0.18, at z≈-4.2.

Wing: elliptical, chord at root ~2.6m, span from centerline to tip 5.6m each side. Wing plane at y≈0.75 (low wing). Tail plane at y≈1.9, z≈-4.0, span 3.2.

Prop: spinner tip at z=+4.9, prop disc radius 1.7 at y≈1.9. Height: prop blade tips reach y≈3.6. Size [11.2, 3.7, 9.8].

Size: width 11.2, height 3.7, length 9.8.

Colors (≤24):
- ink: #0e2a5e deep blueprint blue (main hull)
- inkMid: #1d4a8f lighter blue panel tone
- inkDeep: #081a3d darkest
- paper: #dfeeff white-cyan linework / annotations
- cyan: #3fd6ff glow lines
- cyanDim: #7fb8d9 faded annotation
- steel: maybe gear metal in blueprint tone — keep in blue family: gearBlue #29477e
- propInk: #143366
- accent amber? Blueprint usually mono; keep a faint warm accent maybe not. Keep all blue/white/cyan. Add "grid" #16355f for sheet grid, "sheetBlue" #0d2f63 sheet background... Sheet is big flat plane with grid via paint? Parts are flat colors — grid lines as parts would cost too much. Use paint? Palette limited but paints allowed? The spec format says every surface is one flat colour. Grid could be a texture? Keep it simple: sheet = deep blue with cyan border frame and corner marks as parts; grid via paint is riskier to spec. I'll specify grid as paint on the sheet (paints are allowed in the SDK; the spec's palette is flat colours). I'll mention paint for grid. Or simpler: grid drawn as thin strips — too many parts. Use paint stripes? I'll spec: sheet is one flat deep-blue plane with a cyan border and title block drawn as parts, plus a subtle grid via a paint of fine lines. Fine.

Joints: static model? The system prompt says static models may omit joints. But spec template includes joints. A plane on the ground — static is fine, but propeller could spin? It's a display model; give prop a hinge joint? Joints for a display model: maybe none. Simpler: static, joints: []. But the template shows joints with roles. I'll make it static except maybe prop spin — riggers appreciate. Let me include a root "airframe" joint and a "propHub" hinge, "rudder" hinge maybe. Hmm, if joints exist, the model is rigged; roles must be from list. Prop = "hinge"? Rotating prop is a hinge. I'll do: root joint "airframe" at [0,0,0] role "spine"; "propHub" at [0,1.85,4.55] dir [0,0,1] role "hinge" group "prop". Keep it minimal: 2 joints. Wheels as joints? Could add wheelFL/FR and gear struts, tailWheel for animation. Let's add: wheelFL, wheelFR (role "hinge", group "gear"), tailWheel hinge, rudder hinge. 6 joints. Parts list which joints they ride.

Parts (6):
1. fuselage — nose to tail cone, cockpit, canopy, fillets. Box [-0.9, 0.6, -4.5] to [0.9, 2.35, 3.4]. Budget 220.
2. wings — both elliptical wings, ailerons, radiators, cannon barrels/ports, wingtip lights. Box [-5.6, 0.55, -1.2] to [5.6, 1.5, 2.4]. Budget 220.
3. tail — fin, rudder, tailplane, elevators, tailwheel assembly? Tail wheel under fuselage part? Assign tail wheel to tail part: box [-1.9, 0, -4.6] to [1.9, 2.6, -3.0]. Budget 140.
4. propeller & nose gear of engine — spinner, 5 blades, exhaust stubs, hub. Box [-1.75, 0.35, 3.2] to [1.75, 3.7, 5.0]. Budget 150. Blades: 5 blades from hub radius 0.35 to 1.65, tips reaching y 3.6 at 12 o'clock... Actually blade disc center at y=1.85, radius 1.65 → tips y 3.5. Blade tips at lowest reach y=0.2 — above floor ok (floor false). But blade pointing down reaches y=0.2, fine.
5. landing gear — main struts, wheels, mudguards/spats. Box [-3.0, 0, 0.0] to [3.0, 1.0, 1.4]. floor true. Budget 120.
6. blueprint drafting layer — the sheet on the ground (11.5 × 10 sheet), grid, title block, dimension lines, crosshair roundels, callout labels, section marks. Box [-6.0, 0, -5.2] to [6.0, 0.04, 5.2]. floor true. Budget 150. Hmm but "subject is the hero... scenery only where the brief names them" — the brief is "cyanotype blueprint" style, which I interpret as naming a drafting-sheet presentation. I think it's right for this category. Size it to the plane footprint.

Mounts: 
- noseRing [0,1.85,3.45] where prop spinner meets cowling (fuselage ↔ prop).
- wingRoot [±? ] — wing-fuselage joint: mount "wingRootL" [0.85, 1.05, 0.4] and "wingRootR" [-0.85, 1.05, 0.4]? Mounts are single points; give one per side. Or "wingCenter" [0, 0.95, 0.7]. I'll do wingRootL and wingRootR.
- tailJoint [0, 1.6, -3.9] fin root; tailplane roots.
- gearTopL [2.55, 1.0, 0.75]? Gear strut top attaches to wing underside. Mounts "gearTopL" [2.6, 0.95, 0.85], "gearTopR" [-2.6, 0.95, 0.85], "tailwheelTop" [0, 0.75, -4.2].
- sheet: plane rests on sheet, no mount needed.

Joints order: airframe root first, then children. rudder parent airframe; propHub parent airframe; wheels parent airframe.

Dir for joints: airframe dir [0,1,0]; propHub dir [0,0,1] role hinge; rudder dir [0,0,-1]? Rudder hinge axis vertical — bone dir maybe [0,1,0]. role "hinge". wheelFL at [2.55, 0.55, 0.85], dir [1,0,0] (axle axis), role "hinge", group "gear". Wait: left side is +X. So wheelFL at x=+2.55. Yes.

Wheel position: gear strut rakes outward-down? On Spitfire gear legs rake outward. Wheel x≈±2.7, axle y=0.55 (wheel radius 0.55 → touches floor). Strut top at wing root underside x±1.0, y 0.9. Good.

Tail wheel: small radius 0.2, axle y=0.2, at z=-4.1, x=0.

Budgets: 220+220+140+150+120+150 = 1000 > 900. Adjust: 200+200+130+140+110+160=940. Still >900. Target ≤900: 190+190+130+140+110+140 = 900. Good.

Size [11.2, 3.7, 9.8].

Palette ≤24:
- "blueprintInk": "#123363" main hull blue
- "blueprintDeep": "#0a1f45" shadow/deep panels
- "blueprintMid": "#1e4a86" panel variation
- "cyanote": "#bfe9ff" white-blue line work

- "amber": "#ffb84d"? Blueprint style — maybe a tiny warm accent for the prop tips? Keep mono... A single amber accent could pop ("wow"). I'll include "signalAmber": "#ffb547" for wingtip lights and a title-block stamp. Keep.

10 colors, fine.

Layout description: full silhouette from front to back, stance, style on every part (cyan linework decals, rivet dots, panel seams, glowing section edges, drafting annotations).

Now write parts descriptions with construction guidance: each builder reads system prompt + pitch + spec. Describe: fuselage built from loft/sweep along spine chain, elliptical cross-sections tapering, cowling, cockpit canopy (frame + glass panes in cyan-tinted), cockpit opening, panel lines as thin extruded strips or decals in paper color, rivets as tiny studs scattered, gun ports, exhaust shrouds assigned to prop part or fuselage? Exhaust stubs on cowling sides — put them in the prop/nose part (box covers z 3.2-5.0; exhaust at z≈3.0-3.6 — include in prop part with box to z=3.0). Adjust prop box: [-1.75, 0.3, 2.9] to [1.75, 3.7, 5.0].

Ailerons as thin slabs with hinge gap lines, cannon bulges and barrels protruding from leading edge at z~0.4-0.8, x±2.8 and ±4.0 (two per wing), radiator fairings under wing at x±1.8, retractable... keep static. Wingtip navigation lights as small amber/red discs? Blueprint style: glowing cyan circles. Use glowCyan circles on tips, amber accents.

Tail: fin with rudder (hinge joint rudder), tailplane with elevator, tail wheel + strut from tail part. Blueprint callouts on tail.

Blueprint details everywhere: paper-colored outline strokes along panel edges, dimension lines with arrowheads and tick labels (small extruded text-like bars? Text as decal/texture via svg is allowed — builders know svg from system prompt). I'll mention: labels drawn as svg decals (tiny serif annotations in paper color), crosshair circle markers, rivet dots as tiny studs, panel seams as thin paper strips seated on surface, glowing cyan edges (glowCyan) along wing leading edges and cowling — "Lanterns, fire, crystals, magic and screens glow" — glowing is allowed for magic; blueprint glow lines are fine stylistically.

Sheet: big plane 12×10.4, floor at y=0, painted deep blue with grid paint, border frame in cyan, title block bottom-right with ruled rows, corner registration marks, a few dimension lines running beside the aircraft with arrowheads and tick marks, circled section letters, a north-arrow-like scale. Keep under budget 140-160.

Mounts list:
- "noseRing": [0, 1.5, 3.3] — cowling front face center where spinner roots. Prop hub joint at [0,1.85,3.4]? Spinner axis at y=1.85? Engine axis on Spitfire tilts slightly down but keep horizontal at y=1.85. NoseRing [0,1.85,3.35].
- "wingRootL": [0.95, 1.05, 0.5], "wingRootR": [-0.95, 1.05, 0.5].

- "gearTopL": [1.0, 0.95, 0.85]... hmm strut top on wing underside near x=1.0? Actually Spitfire gear attaches near wing root, wheels track ~2.4m. Let strut top at x=±1.6, y=0.85, z=0.8; wheel axle at x=±2.55, y=0.55, z=0.95. Mounts gearTopL/R at [±1.6, 0.85, 0.8].

4. gearFL parent airframe at [1.6, 0.85, 0.8], dir [1,0,0], role "hinge"? Legs are legs — role "leg"? A gear leg is a leg chain. Use role "leg", group "gear", names gearFL/gearFR. Wheels: wheelFL parent gearFL? Simpler: gearL, gearR, tailWheel as three leg-role chains each single joint, wheel as separate hinge joints children. Let's do:

Tail part includes tail wheel which rests on floor! But I put tail wheel in tail part... Then tail part floor: true. Hmm, or tail wheel in landing gear part — landing gear box z range must extend to -4.6. Gear box: [-3.0, 0, -4.6] to [3.0, 1.0, 1.4]. Fine, gear part owns tail wheel. Then tail floor false.
